P1.evidence: Setter notes read back and then used three separate times as discovery scaffolding — the yoga certification, the weight goal, and the general situation — which is the check working as designed and which drew an important correction: the setter recorded 20-30lb and the prospect said 'honestly I probably have to lose like 60 or 70 pounds.' The frame carried two of four parts and agreement was only a trailing 'Sounds good.' The open question ran well.

P2.evidence: Three strong hits and one conspicuous absence. The training week was asked properly and produced an unusually complete picture — 10k steps, sauna five or six days, an hour of yoga six days, tai chi, twice-daily meditation. Diet was asked twice and walked through in real detail. Sleep was asked directly — 'What's your sleep schedule look like actually right now?' — and pursued into the wake-at-3am pattern, which turned out to be the central physiological fact of the call. The gap: occupation was never asked at any point, so after 62 minutes the record cannot say what this man does for a living. Age, height and weight were never asked either, on a call whose stated goal is losing 60-70lb. Health conditions and injuries are partial only because the prospect volunteered flat feet, an uneven gait, infant leg bracing, former acid reflux and chronic bloating into gaps the rep left; none of it was asked for.

P3.evidence: The bridge question ran in clean scripted form — 'how would you say, like, what's your biggest why behind this? Why you want to do this?' — and produced three minutes of unguarded answer covering the platform he is building, leadership, longevity, his mother's death from Alzheimer's, and service. The rep then delivered the best reflect-back in the batch: 'So it's not about losing weight, actually. It's way more than that. Like, losing weight is just like a byproduct', confirmed with 'Yeah, exactly.' Legacy and identity were fully reached. Earlier he had also asked the excellent open diagnostic 'you're doing a lot, like 10k steps a day, sauna, yoga, so what's missing?', which drew the prospect's own answer: a personalised approach, community, accountability and feedback. What did not run: no aesthetics question, no explicit who-else-does-this-impact, and the can't-do material arrived unasked.

P4.evidence: One short question did most of the work: 'What happened with the push-ups?' That opened the entire recovery problem and, through it, the estate, the sleep disruption and the cortisol state. The blocker was named precisely and by the prospect — 'I'm not recovering well, it's a bit like the bottom line to the question, like my sleep is not really where it needs to be' — and he named the gap himself when asked what was missing. What never ran was the sequence proper: no 'what have you tried before', no 'why do you feel it didn't stick', and no version of the information-isn't-the-problem move, which would have landed unusually well on a man who says he knows a lot about fitness and does not look it.

P5.evidence: Never run, and here that is defensible on judgement rather than a simple omission. The prospect was describing acute ongoing distress, and a scripted consequence frame — what does the next two years look like, are you willing to settle — would have been the wrong instrument. But some version was needed, because when the money objection arrived there was nothing to weigh a seven-week delay against, and the rep had nothing to reach for but a $100 deposit.

P6.evidence: The all-in question ran and ran well, with the identity hook attached and tuned to what he had just heard: 'are you fully in on doing the work to become that guy, the guy whose body reflects the effort that he's already putting in?' The answer was a hedge — 'I would say so' — followed immediately by a stated doubt: 'general fear or doubt of like, can I really do this?' The rep did the right thing next and asked 'And why is that?', which produced the most important disclosure of the call. Then he did the wrong thing: the script says do not move forward without a clear yes and return to Phase 5 if hesitation surfaces, and he moved straight to price with the doubt explicitly open. P6c is a clean miss, and it is why the close never had a foundation.

P11.evidence: None of the four steps completed. The $6,000 was not collected — only a $100 refundable deposit, which is a booking fee rather than a payment. No onboarding call with Trevor was scheduled; the September 14 slot is with the rep. No agreement was sent or mentioned. No welcome email, no Skool, no onboarding form. The rep did close out responsibly, advising the prospect to keep to simple foundational movements and to swap tai chi for mobility work in the interim, which is good relationship management but is not P11.

objection_plays.detail: The isolation move ran, late but in an unusually honest register: 'let's zoom out for a second. Let's take a chill pill... let's just talk about like real talk about money. Cause is it, is it like, if it's like a money concern issue right now for you that you don't have this money, that's fine. Just, you can say it to me. Like I'm a grown man and I can accept it.' That produced a full and truthful picture — receivables owed under contract, estate taxes, pre-sale repairs to roof, siding, landscaping, driveway and plumbing, and a large payment expected in early September. The credit score question ran. The payment ladder ran. What did not: no should-versus-how frame, no cash on hand, no card count, no available credit, no investments, and no attempt to size a first payment against the September receipt. The rep also volunteered the de-pressuring 'I don't want you to pick between joining this and not having food on the table', which is humane and which also removed any remaining urgency.

A clear trigger — 'Could I touch base with you in a month or something and just start from there and do what I'm doing now and kind of pick up? Is this like you're not going to be accepting clients in a couple of months?' Not one OD move ran. No things-never-slow-down, no when-does-it-actually-become-the-right-time, no compounding-cost, no 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled' — which is the single line best matched to a man whose stated problem is that he makes too many decisions a day. The rep moved in the opposite direction and actively de-escalated. Given the disclosed distress that is a defensible human choice, but the seven-week gap it produced depends on third parties paying him and a house selling, and the play existed to test exactly that.

The trigger was explicit and self-diagnosed: 'general fear or doubt of like, can I really do this?' followed by 'I've lost a bit of confidence in myself, despite having a good work ethic.' The rep's first move was the right one and is not in the script — he asked why, and then let a long answer run without interrupting. His response was the promise-keeping reframe: making a promise to yourself and keeping it builds confidence and improves relationships. None of the scripted OE moves ran — no certainty question, no pleasure-versus-pain, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before, no 'how will you know if you never actually try'. The doubt was heard and honoured and never actually resolved, and it was still open when the call ended.

SCRIPT GAP — a prospect disclosing severe ongoing psychological distress. Chronic sleep disruption with nightmares, a self-described constant fight-or-flight state, social isolation, repeated experiences of rock bottom, and six years of exposure to material he has to identify and destroy. The playbook has nothing for this, and the rep improvised toward the sale: 'this is going to be like a part of work on yourself too.' He handled the human side well — he listened, he did not exploit it, and he declined to press at the close. But a prospect in this state needs a boundary line the script does not supply, and the only thing offered was a fitness programme and a $100 deposit. This belongs to the principal as a policy question, not to the rep as a coaching note.

notes: The best goals phase and the best reflect-back in the batch, attached to a close that never had a foundation because P6c was ignored — a stated 'can I really do this?' went straight to a price conversation instead of back to Phase 5. Two things to escalate rather than coach. First, the renewal rate was disclosed here at $3,000 for a further six months, and that is the same number quoted as an initial price on the Bennu call four days earlier; the principal should establish whether reps are using the renewal rate as a discount. Second, the script has no guidance for a prospect disclosing acute psychological distress, and this rep filled that vacuum by positioning the programme as part of the repair. He behaved decently throughout; the gap is structural.
